_purpose: Machine-readable actor-based flows สำหรับ AI/coding tools — generate test cases, unit tests, automation
_status: Generated from PDT-3562-uc1b-complete-jira-story.json (Layer 2 STEP 6, 2026-07-09 — NOT signed off). UC1b = the 'Live' player component (QA-internal split of PDT-3562 by player component).
_warning: FU-2 (central button hit-target) is PENDING and the web-Live reveal-controls overlay is NET-NEW (DEV-DELTA — bare Plyr pause/play only today). Flows touching these carry assumption flags — NOT blocked. There is NO resume flow in UC1b: live resume-to-live is owned by UC2.

actors.viewer: Community member watching a 'Live' live stream (Room status: live)
actors.app: Host app shell that mounts the Live player in a feed/fullscreen surface and bridges OS lifecycle
actors.player: The 'Live' player component (UC1b) — controls overlay reveal/dismiss, central pause/play button + icon, 1s auto-dismiss timer, seek-control presence. NET-NEW on web-Live.
actors.sdk: Amity SDK / live stream engine — true playback state (playing/paused/buffering), room status (live), live edge
actors.network: Network layer between the player and the live stream source — stalls cause buffering
actors.system: OS / platform runtime — app background/foreground lifecycle, OS-level media pause

flows.name: Default baseline — active Live before any tap
flows.summary: A 'Live' stream renders with the standing LIVE badge and viewer count and NO controls overlay before the first tap

steps.action: opens a feed/post containing an actively broadcasting 'Live' stream and performs no tap yet
mounts the Live player component on the current surface (inline feed or fullscreen)
reports room status = live with playback active
renders the live video surface with the standing LIVE badge and viewer count and NO controls overlay

state_change.value: hidden (baseline — LIVE badge + viewer count shown)

unit: render Live player with sdk room_status=live and no tap → assert controls overlay NOT present in the view/DOM
assert LIVE badge and viewer-count element are visible at baseline
scenario: open a feed with an active Live post → verify only video + LIVE badge + viewer count, no overlay before interaction
e2e: load a Live post → before any interaction assert no controls overlay and LIVE badge present

flows.name: Tap reveals controls (mobile) — playback continues
flows.summary: On mobile (iOS / Android / web-on-mobile) the first tap reveals the controls overlay WITHOUT toggling playback; the stream keeps playing and the central pause icon is shown

assumptions.text: web-Live reveal-controls overlay is NET-NEW — no existing implementation (LIVE path today is a bare <video>+Plyr with pause/play only, LivestreamPlayer.tsx). Build + verify from scratch, not against existing behaviour.

steps.action: taps anywhere on the playing 'Live' player surface (mobile: iOS / Android / web-on-mobile)
reveals the controls overlay WITHOUT issuing pause/play — mobile first-tap is reveal-only
keeps playback running uninterrupted — no pause is issued by the reveal
shows the central pause icon, reflecting the still-playing state
starts the 1s idle auto-dismiss countdown (see flow-UC1b-F05)

unit: mock a playing Live stream on mobile → simulate tap → assert overlay visible AND sdk playback still playing (NOT paused)
assert central button icon = pause after reveal
scenario: iOS / Android / web-mobile: tap a playing Live player → verify controls appear and the stream keeps playing
e2e: web-mobile — tap the Live player → assert overlay appears and video.paused === false
web-Live overlay is net-new — verify from scratch, not against any existing overlay behaviour

flows.name: Desktop variant — 1-Step Pause (platform split BR-09)
flows.summary: On desktop (Web UIKit) the first tap is a direct 1-Step Pause — it does NOT use the mobile reveal-controls path; playback pauses immediately

steps.action: taps the playing 'Live' player once on desktop (Web UIKit)
routes the tap to a direct 1-Step Pause (desktop interaction model), NOT reveal-only
pauses playback — on desktop a single tap toggles pause/play directly
shows the play icon, reflecting the paused state

unit: desktop Web UIKit — simulate tap on a playing Live player → assert direct pause (playback paused), NOT a reveal-only outcome
scenario: desktop browser — single tap on a playing Live player → verify it pauses immediately (1-step); the mobile reveal path is not used
e2e: desktop viewport — click the Live player once → assert video.paused === true; contrast with the mobile reveal path (flow-UC1b-F02)
platform split is BR-09: never author one shared cross-platform expected for the first-tap AC

flows.name: Tap outside button (playing) — overlay dismisses, playback continues
flows.summary: With the overlay visible and the stream playing, tapping outside the central button dismisses the overlay while playback continues

assumptions.text: Central pause/play button hit-target size/spec is not yet defined (FU-2, Owner: Design). The pause-vs-dismiss boundary test is non-deterministic until specified; tests assume a tap clearly outside the button's visible bounds dismisses.

steps.action: taps the player surface OUTSIDE the central pause/play button's tap target (overlay visible, stream playing)
dismisses the controls overlay
keeps playback running — a tap outside the button is not a pause

unit: overlay visible + playing → simulate tap outside the button bounds → assert overlay hidden AND playback still playing
scenario: reveal controls, tap a corner of the player away from the central button → verify overlay disappears and the stream keeps playing
e2e: reveal overlay → click clearly outside the central button → assert overlay gone and video.paused === false
FU-2 (button hit-target) is undefined — pick a tap point clearly outside the visible button until the spec lands

flows.name: No action 1s (playing) — overlay auto-dismisses
flows.summary: With the overlay visible and the stream playing, 1 second of no interaction auto-dismisses the overlay; playback continues

steps.action: takes no further action for 1 second while the overlay is visible and the stream is playing
after 1s of no interaction, auto-dismisses the controls overlay
keeps playback running — auto-dismiss does not affect playback

unit: overlay visible + playing → advance the timer 1000ms with no interaction → assert overlay hidden and playback unaffected
scenario: reveal controls, wait 1s without touching → verify the overlay auto-hides and the stream is still playing
e2e: reveal overlay, wait 1s → assert overlay gone
web-Live overlay + auto-dismiss timer is net-new — verify from scratch; web currently uses 3000ms and MUST be changed to 1s (iOS is already 1s)

flows.name: Idle timer resets on control interaction
flows.summary: Interacting with an overlay control before the 1s timeout restarts the countdown; the overlay does not disappear mid-interaction and dismisses 1s after the last interaction

steps.action: interacts with an overlay control before the 1s timeout elapses
restarts the 1s idle countdown on the interaction — the overlay does NOT disappear while interacting
stops interacting with the overlay
auto-dismisses the overlay 1s after the last interaction

unit: overlay visible → fire a control interaction at 800ms → assert overlay still visible at 1000ms (timer reset); assert overlay hidden 1000ms after the last interaction
scenario: reveal controls, tap a control every ~0.8s → verify the overlay stays; stop → verify it hides ~1s later
e2e: reveal overlay, interact just before 1s several times → assert overlay persists; then idle → assert it hides after 1s

flows.name: Tap pause on Live — pauses, play icon persists, NO seek controls, tap-outside stays paused
flows.summary: Tapping the central pause button pauses the Live stream; the play icon persists; NO ±10s seek controls appear (Live has none — BR-01); a subsequent tap-outside dismisses the overlay and the stream stays paused. Resume-to-live is owned by UC2 — not authored here.

steps.action: taps the central pause button (controls overlay visible, stream playing)
pauses live playback
switches the central button icon pause→play and keeps it visible
shows NO seek/skip (±10s) controls — a Live stream has no seek controls
taps anywhere outside the play button
dismisses the overlay — a paused overlay dismisses only on a tap outside the play button
leaves playback paused — the stream stays paused (NO resume here; resume-to-live is owned by UC2)

unit: playing Live + overlay visible → tap the central pause → assert playback paused, icon = play persists, and assert NO seek buttons appear on the Live pause overlay (BR-01)
assert no ±10s / back-forward skip elements are rendered on the Live overlay in any state
scenario: pause a Live stream → verify the play icon stays and verify NO seek buttons appear on the Live pause overlay; tap outside → verify overlay hides and the stream is still paused
e2e: reveal → tap pause → assert video.paused === true, play icon visible, seek buttons absent; tap outside → assert overlay hidden and video still paused
do NOT test resume here — resume-to-live is UC2

flows.name: Behaviour identical across in-scope surfaces (surface-invariant)
flows.summary: The AC-01…AC-04 interactions behave identically whether the Live stream is inline in a feed or in fullscreen/gallery view (surface-invariant, NOT platform-invariant)

steps.action: performs the AC-01…AC-04 interactions (reveal, tap-outside dismiss, 1s auto-dismiss, pause) on a 'Live' stream playing INLINE in a feed
on the inline surface behaves per flow-UC1b-F02 / F04 / F05 / F07
repeats the same interactions on the same 'Live' stream in FULLSCREEN / gallery view
on the fullscreen surface behaves IDENTICALLY to the inline surface

unit: parametrize the reveal/dismiss/auto-dismiss/pause tests over surface = [inline, fullscreen] → assert identical outcomes
scenario: run the full UC1b interaction matrix on the inline feed then in fullscreen → verify no behavioural difference
e2e: inline vs fullscreen — reveal / dismiss / pause on both → assert identical results
BR-06 is surface-invariant, NOT platform-invariant — desktop still differs (flow-UC1b-F03)

flows.name: Pause tap coincides with auto-dismiss timer firing (race)
flows.summary: When the user taps pause at the exact instant the 1s idle timer would fire, the pause wins — playback pauses, the play icon persists, and the overlay is NOT swallowed by the expiring timer

steps.action: the 1s idle auto-dismiss timer is about to fire (overlay visible, stream playing)
taps the central pause button at that exact instant
pauses playback
shows and KEEPS the play icon — the pause is not swallowed by the expiring timer
keeps the overlay visible — it dismisses only on a subsequent tap-outside (a paused overlay persists)

unit: set the timer to fire at t=1000ms and dispatch the pause at t=1000ms → assert final state paused + play icon visible + overlay still shown (not auto-dismissed)
scenario: reveal controls, wait ~1s, tap pause exactly as it would auto-hide → verify it pauses and the overlay stays (paused state wins the race)
e2e: reveal → wait ~950ms → tap pause → assert paused, play icon persists, overlay visible until a tap-outside

flows.name: Tap during buffering / stall
flows.summary: While the Live stream is buffering (not yet playing), a tap reveals the overlay with the central button reflecting the REAL state — never a false 'playing' icon — with no crash or frozen overlay

steps.action: the live stream stalls — data underruns / connection is poor
reports the stream as buffering (not yet playing)
taps the player surface during buffering
reveals the overlay; the central button reflects the real (buffering) state, NOT a false 'playing' icon
surfaces an explicit state — no crash and no frozen overlay

unit: mock sdk state = buffering → simulate tap → assert overlay shown, central button reflects buffering (NOT a false pause/playing icon), no exception thrown
scenario: throttle the network to force buffering on a Live stream → tap → verify the overlay appears with the correct state, no crash/freeze
e2e: use network throttling / route stall to force buffering → tap the player → assert overlay + correct state indicator
web-Live overlay is net-new — verify from scratch

flows.name: App backgrounded during an active overlay/timer (OS default)
flows.summary: Backgrounding the app mid-countdown and returning leaves the player/overlay in a well-defined state via the OS default (Option 1) with no stale mid-countdown overlay. Foreground snap-to-live is UC2's rule — not asserted here.

steps.action: sends the app to the background while the controls overlay is visible (mid-countdown)
OS suspends the app; iOS pauses AVPlayer (no background-audio mode); web delegates to the browser's native <video>/HLS.js
returns the app to the foreground
resumes and re-attaches the Live player view

reaches a well-defined state via the OS default (Option 1) — the 1s auto-dismiss timer is wall-clock, so a playing overlay is already dismissed on return and a paused overlay persists; no stale mid-countdown overlay

unit: assert the 1s auto-dismiss timer is wall-clock so no mid-countdown overlay survives backgrounding; assert no explicit background handler forces a spurious state (code-verified: neither repo handles backgrounding — delegated to OS)
scenario: reveal overlay → background the app for >1s → foreground → verify no stale mid-countdown overlay; player in a well-defined state
e2e: iOS / Android — background then foreground with the overlay up → assert no frozen/stale overlay
do NOT assert resume-to-live here — that is UC2
